title: This Almost Broke Me… | Ring of Recoil vs Velgar (RuneScape Dragonwilds)
author: SuperStooob
chapters: How the Ring of Recoil Actually Works
description:
I tried to kill Velgar using ONLY the Ring of Recoil in RuneScape Dragonwilds - no real weapons, no damage dealt directly.

What started as a stupid idea quickly turned into one of the most brutal and mentally draining fights I’ve done in Dragonwilds. Between potion math, poison damage, failed attempts, and learning Velgar’s mechanics the hard way… this almost broke me.

This video is a full narrative journey: testing the Ring of Recoil on weaker enemies, scaling up through harder fights, and finally putting it to the ultimate test against Velgar.

If you’re playing RuneScape Dragonwilds and wondering how far game mechanics can be pushed - this is for you.

00:00 – How the Ring of Recoil Actually Works
00:16 - The Idea that Shouldn't Work
00:28 – Testing It on Weak Enemies
01:21 – Scaling Up the Difficulty
02:04 – The First Serious Problem

05:45– What Went Wrong

08:15 – Victory (and Why This Hurt)

transcript.text: I wasn't even farming this for a video, I was killing green dragons when both vestiges dropped at
once and one of those vestiges makes the ring of recoil. It reflects 50 % of the damage you take back to the
attack at which means in theory you don't need a weapon, you just need to survive.
So the question stopped being can this work and became how far can I take it? Velgar has 3000 health and if this ring
works the way it says it does, I shouldn't need to him even once. So I need to improve the concept. I started small.
First off, a level 1 Kebbit. It worked. Then a cow, which when I realised this wasn't
going to be fast, by the time I reached Goblins it was obvious what the trade-off was.
The ring does damage but it charges interest. Every hit you take deals damage back but you always pay more than you get.
So I kept moving forward and moved on to the gurus and they taught me so much because
to an unarmoured player they do so much damage and they often do attacks in quick succession.
I definitely started becoming more strategic and told me exactly what this Velgar fight
is going to be about health management, arm management and a whole lot of patience. So at this point I felt comfortable.
Stay alive, drink potions, let the ring do the work. Then I decided to push it. Enter the Abyssal Demon.
And honestly, it was working. All I had to do was stay alive, not take too many hits in a row,
and slowly but surely the Abyssal Demon would kill itself. So things was going great, until it wasn't.
I got blind during the fight, then a poison rat, and suddenly I wasn't testing a mechanic anymore.
I was watching everything collapse.
And that's really mattered because it showed me the real cost. Velgar, as we know, has 3000 health. Lesser potions
they heal 70, which means even in perfect conditions I need around 100 potions. That's assuming no waste, no poison,
no mistakes. So I made 200. So confidence high, bag full of potions and gear,
heading over to Velgar's Tower with the challenge horn ready for this monumental task.
The rules of engagement were simple, stand close, get hit, drink,
repeat. Every quarter health felt that he's got to fly up, poison the arena and then come back down.
I need to avoid that poison to avoid taking too much damage. And the fight was going fine, the plan was working.
And then I noticed something I completely forgot. This is a survival game. I didn't bring water.
Oh my god, such a new mistake. How could I forget to even bring water along? So many other things going on in my mind,
I forgot about the most simplest things. Hydration. I could have pushed on, but dying at the end would have wasted
everything. All these potions I didn't want to risk it. So I jumped losing the fight
was better than losing these potions. And after a few more back and forths we
felt our wasting resources and being sent back to my home in Bramblemead every single time.
If I controlled my arm appropriately I could control how much damage he dealt. That's gonna save me so much in potions.
I could get him to do 69 that's one potion, one hit repeat. That makes the fight so simple and it
just involved wearing the paladin helmet, and paladin platelegs. I had the plan. It was slow but it was stable.
That's what I needed at this point. So I knew what I had to do.
I had to keep on trying. And then it happened. First phase done.
Second phase done. Third phase done.
We're on to the fourth phase. I made it to the final phase.
I'm shaking. It's been a 15 minute fight so far. Even on this fourth phase something happened
which I knew was going to happen. I got poisoned but I referred to my training. I planned for this prepared for it.
Just took the anti poison and moved on. Everything was fine. I was ready to end the fight. And then it happened.
Fourth phase. Almost done. I can see the light at the end of the tunnel. Velgar reared up, slammed down,
shock waves under my feet. I died at the end.
So close. So much time making potion, so much time on the fight just to get to this point of fail again.
I'm about to give up. I decided to go on a test run. I'm gonna take my fallen hoplite blade and I still sword.
I'm gonna get to the fourth phase again and see if I can recreate it and find out why that
mechanic happened and killed me in such a devastating way. So I needed to understand what went wrong.
I went back in fully geared, sword, armor, no risk. And that's when I confirmed it.
This shockwave only triggers if you stand too far back, which meant the death wasn't bad luck. It was positioning.
And that's perfect because that's something I can fix. There's something I can work on.
I took a couple of days off and I just couldn't get this challenge out of my head.
So I rebuilt 250 potions made for one fight. This time I played it safe.
I was gonna bring my armor for the final phase just in case you did that again. No rush in, no greed,
just execution.
At 15 minutes later I was back on the final phase. No poison, no mistakes and I'm here. I'm ready.
I'm ready to finish this fight. The problem wearing the hoplite
was it was just too slow So I decided to risk it all. I'm going back to the Paladin and I'm going to finish what
I started.
got sweaty, all this work hours days put into this moment and then after 17 minutes 150 potions felt god died without
me swinging once the ring of recoil did its job
it's not overpowered it's slow it's expensive and it punishes mistakes but if you respect the system it works
I was victorious. I was relieved, but I do have a problem because if this works on Velgar,
I can't pretend I'm not thinking about Imaru
